newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mayne say Seven serves notice on Optus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mayne say Seven serves notice on Optus.

text.p: Mayne Nickless Ltd said on Tuesday that Seven Network Ltd would serve a default notice on Optus Vision.
Mayne Nickless said the notice depends on the outcome of the litigation between Seven and Optus Vision, which is to be heard in the Supreme Court of New South Wales on February 24, 1997.

"Optus Communications Pty Limited has confirmed that pursuant to the Optus Vision Shareholders' Agreement, Tallglen Pty Ltd (a subsidiary of Seven Network Ltd) has served a default acquisition notice on Optus Communications in respect of its 46.5 percent shareholding in Optus Vision Pty Ltd," Mayne said.
Mayne Nickless owns about 25 percent of Optus Communications and Seven Network owns a two percent stake in Optus Vision, a pay television group.
Mayne said the notice arose out of the current dispute between Tallglen and the other shareholders of Optus Vision.

Tallglen's right to serve such a notice depends on the outcome of the litigation concerning the dispute which is set down to be heard in the Supreme Court of New South Wales commencing on February 24, 1997, Mayne Nickless said.

It said if Tallglen is successful in the litigation it would allow Tallglen to acquire Optus Communications stake in Optus Vision shares at a price which is equal to 85 percent of the lower of cost and the average of the special purpose valuation under the Optus Vision Shareholders' Agreement.
